texts.preamble: Amal Chanda & Anr vs Superintendent Of Police on 24 March, 2025 24.03.2025 Sl. no. 18 Ct. No. 237 P.M. C.R.R. 1881 Of 2023 Amal Chanda & Anr. - vs - Superintendent of Police, Barasat Police & Ors. Mr. Dhrubaneel Biswas, Ms. Susmita Hazra, Mr. Sandeepan Dutta ... for the petitioners
texts.facts: This is an application wherein petitioners have challenged the proceeding being Duttapukur P.S. Case No. 202 of 2017 for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 272/273/420 of the Indian Penal Code read with Section 103/104/108 of the Trademarks Act, 1999, presently pending before the learned 5th Additional District and Sessions Judge, Barasat being S.C. Case No. 116 of 2020. Petitioners contended that respondents have no jurisdiction to raid the factory or business place of the petitioners without any competent Food Safety Officer and he also did not follow the protocol for collecting samples and they also did not give any opportunity to prefer appeal as the samples has already been degraded before it was sent to testing lab. Furthermore, the respondents arranged the witnesses prior to conduct the said raid and further collected the food samples in the absence of the petitioner No. 1.
texts.arguments: His main contention is that due to massive delay in sending of samples to the lab which is after about 24 days, the collected samples were degraded and as such the proceeding initiated against them is not sustainable in the eye of law. Having heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioners the application is admitted.
texts.petitioner_arguments: His main contention is that due to massive delay in sending of samples to the lab which is after about 24 days, the collected samples were degraded and as such the proceeding initiated against them is not sustainable in the eye of law. Having heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioners the application is admitted.
